findings.title: The folder note does not offer the full flow, and no test checks that it does
quotes: then `nio check tasks` prints a note naming the folders and the full flow
findings.fix: add the offer text from CT-4 to the note and assert it in `test_lite_escalate_note`

sources.situation: the note the code prints ends "consider a full spec". CT-4 asks for "offer the full flow (@nio:spec, "Escalating a bug fix")". The test only checks `startswith("escalate: the fix changes files in 2 folders (src/a, src/a/sub)")`, so a note that drops the offer still passes.

a lite effort whose tasks span two folders gets `escalate: the fix changes files in 2 folders (src/a, src/a/sub); consider a full spec`. CT-4 asks for the offer of the full flow with the `@nio:spec` pointer, and AC-9 says the note names "the full flow". The code's wording calls it "a full spec", and the test only checks the prefix, so the mismatch passes unnoticed.

a lite effort touches two folders. The note says "consider a full spec" and does not name the offer or the spec skill's "Escalating a bug fix" section. AC-9 says the check prints `escalate:` with each folder "and the offer of the full flow". `test_lite_escalate_note` asserts only the prefix up to the folder list, so it passes anyway.

findings.reason: src/nio/tasks.py:276 prints `...; consider a full spec`, not CT-4's `: offer the full flow (@nio:spec, "Escalating a bug fix")`, and tests/test_tasks.py:580 (`test_lite_escalate_note`) asserts only the prefix up to the folder list, so the missing offer passes unnoticed. Nothing else in the spec settles the wording; AC-9 requires the offer of the full flow.

findings.title: The agent-judged folder trigger drops the non-test qualifier that FR-8 and AC-9 keep
quotes: changes non-test files in more than one folder
files in more than one folder;
findings.fix: add "non-test" to the spec skill's trigger list and to the tasks skill description (and to CT-12's implement wording if it is meant to match), so the agent and the CLI apply the same rule.

sources.situation: a lite fix changes `src/a/x.py` and `tests/test_x.py`. `nio check tasks` gives no note, since the test file is left out of the count (AC-9's own example). The spec skill's escalation list still says "files in more than one folder", so the agent stops and offers the full flow for a change FR-8 does not cover, and the tasks skill description repeats the same unqualified trigger. The spec and the CLI disagree on the same case.

findings.reason: FR-8 and AC-9 say "non-test files", and tasks.py excludes test paths from the count. skills/spec/SKILL.md:84 says "files in more than one folder;" and skills/tasks/SKILL.md:3 says "files in more than one folder" with no qualifier, and nothing nearby settles it. An agent following the skill would escalate on `src/a/x.py` plus `tests/test_x.py`, where the CLI gives no note.

findings.title: The folder count skips `file_of`, so a Files entry with no file path counts as a folder
findings.fix: pass each entry through `file_of` and drop the None results before taking `PurePosixPath(...).parent`, as CT-4 says.

sources.situation: CT-4 builds the list from `files` then `file_of`, and `file_of` returns None for an entry with no file-like path. The code uses `files` alone, so a `Files:` entry such as `src/a/x.py, none` yields the parent `.` for `none` and reports two folders (`.` and `src/a`), giving a spurious escalate note. This is inferred from reading the helpers; I did not run it.

findings.title: Files entries are not run through file_of
findings.fix: map each entry through `file_of`, skip None, then take the parent

sources.situation: the folder set is built from the raw `files(...)` entries, not from `file_of`. An entry with trailing words that contain a slash, such as `src/a/x.py see docs/notes`, yields a bogus parent folder and a false or missed escalation. An entry naming no file, such as `docs`, counts as the root folder `.`.
